title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Colorado confirms foreign actors changed settings, silenced alarms and altered pumping at two small water systems
items.content_text: Colorado’s Governor’s office said on 18 September that foreign actors breached two small, privately owned drinking-water providers in late August. Once inside, they changed equipment settings, disabled alarms and remote access, and altered pumping cycles. The state says the disruptions were brief, the providers corrected them and alerted the state, and there was no known effect on water treatment, water quality or public safety; the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment confirmed the problems were resolved, and the state has told other providers to review their security. The office would not say who was responsible, while noting federal awareness of an Iranian-backed group targeting US water systems. This is the shape of the national campaign against internet-exposed water controllers (see the CISA card below), now with hands-on process tampering confirmed by a state government. The consequence was small this time — each utility serves fewer than 200 residents — but at a system that size, the alarm is often the only operator on shift.

_otthreatfeed.category: Top Story

items.title: A third energy carrier reports a suspected attack at sea — while the one confirmed compromise still has no named actor
items.content_text: A third energy carrier in about a month has reported a suspected cyberattack at sea. Bloomberg reported on 18 September that the crew of the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG, loaded with US cargo and bound for Italy, lost access to some internal control systems and diverted; the Italian Coast Guard cites a cargo-monitoring malfunction with no cause established. It follows the FBI and Coast Guard boarding two US-bound tankers in late August after both vessels’ networks were found compromised; the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, has since named the second as the LPG carrier Kohaku. Rear Adm. Amy Grable, who commands Coast Guard Cyber Command, says investigators did find malicious cyber activity aboard the crude carrier VL Prosperity, but no operational disruption; claims that hackers seized navigation and propulsion come from Iranian state media and remain unverified. For OT defenders the point stands: a vessel is a mobile control-system site that berths against your terminal, and nobody inspects its network.
tags: Incident — confirmed network compromise aboard two US-bound tankers, no confirmed operational disruption; a third carrier’s incident is suspected

items.title: More than a hundred water systems, one campaign, and the only thing the attackers needed was a PLC facing the internet
items.content_text: CISA has confirmed that over 100 US water and wastewater systems were targeted during July, in a campaign federal agencies attribute to Iran-affiliated actors and characterise as opportunistic rather than selective. The technique was not sophisticated: find a programmable logic controller reachable from the public internet, change its password and its network settings, and lock the operator out of their own equipment. Some utilities reported flooding and drops in water pressure afterwards. Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers were named first; the joint advisory has since been widened to Schneider Electric and Siemens devices, with the actors also using vendors’ own engineering software — Studio 5000, EcoStruxure Control Expert, TIA Portal — to pull project files out of victim environments. This is the clearest confirmed OT-disruptive campaign in the current window, and none of it required a vulnerability. On 18 September Colorado confirmed two more small providers had equipment settings, alarms and pumping cycles tampered with in late August, attacker not confirmed (see top story).
tags: Incident — confirmed OT compromise of internet-exposed PLCs across more than 100 US water systems

items.title: The router at the unmanned site can be taken over the SSH port without a password — and it was being taken a day before the fix shipped
items.content_text: CERT Polska coordinated disclosure of six RouterOS vulnerabilities and confirmed that two of them, chained, give an unauthenticated attacker full control of any MikroTik device with SSH reachable from the internet. The chain — CVE-2026-67276, an SSH authentication bypass, with CVE-2026-86060, a session privilege manipulation flaw triggered by specially crafted usernames — is being actively exploited, with activity observed from at least 2 September, a day before MikroTik shipped patched builds. The Shadowserver Foundation counted roughly 122,500 RouterOS devices with SSH exposed in a single 24-hour scan. MikroTik gear is not an OT product, which is exactly the problem: it is the cheap, capable router that turns up at wellpads, pump stations, substations and remote skids, often installed by an integrator and never entered into an asset register. A useful indicator of compromise is an SSH user literally named “-2”.
tags: Incident — confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of chained SSH flaws in edge routers

items.title: During an active support session, someone can push a file to your machine and run it — no authorisation, no prompt
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 September after confirming in-the-wild attacks, with a federal remediation deadline of 14 September under BOD 26-04. The flaw — improper privilege management combined with missing authorisation, rated CVSS 9.9 — lets an attacker transfer a file to a device during an active remote session and execute it without the host user authorising or even being asked. ConnectWise patched on 8 September. ScreenConnect is the tool a very large number of system integrators, OEM service organisations and managed service providers use to reach industrial customers, which means the affected device is frequently an engineering workstation or an HMI server sitting inside a plant network, and the session is one the site itself invited.
tags: Incident — confirmed exploitation of remote support software used by integrators and managed service providers

items.title: More than five hundred ICS advisories in a single year — and the flaws that never get one are the more severe half
items.content_text: Forescout’s analysis of fifteen years of industrial advisory data found ICS advisory volume passing 500 in a year for the first time, carrying 2,155 CVEs, against 67 advisories and 103 CVEs in 2011. Average advisory severity has climbed from roughly 6.4 in 2010 to above 8.0 in the last two years, and the affected gear sits mostly at Purdue levels 1 to 3 — controllers, engineering software and supervisory systems in manufacturing, energy, transport, healthcare and water. The finding that matters operationally is the blind spot: of industrial-product vulnerabilities published without a corresponding CISA ICS advisory, 61% were rated high or critical. Asset owners who track only the ICS advisory feed are, by the vendor’s count, seeing well under half the severe issues in their own equipment.
tags: Research — Forescout Vedere Labs, ICS advisory and CVE analysis

items.title: Twelve ways into a Siemens edge box, and four of them are reachable by malformed PROFINET discovery traffic
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks Labs published research on the Siemens SCALANCE LPE9403, a local processing engine used as an industrial edge device, identifying twelve vulnerabilities in firmware below V4.0 HF0 — privilege escalation, path traversal, authentication bypass, command injection, buffer overflows and memory-handling issues, with CVSS scores between 5.3 and 8.5. Several can be chained to obtain root. Separately, an emulation-driven fuzzing campaign against the device’s PROFINET Discovery and basic Configuration Protocol implementation — built from process snapshots, the Unicorn CPU emulator and AFL++ — turned up four memory-corruption flaws, CVE-2025-40575 through CVE-2025-40578, each rated CVSS 4.0 5.3: an uninitialised value, a NULL pointer dereference and two out-of-bounds reads. The DCP flaws matter disproportionately because DCP is unauthenticated link-layer traffic: anything on the PROFINET segment can send it.
tags: Vendor research — Nozomi Networks Labs; twelve flaws in a Siemens industrial edge device, chainable to root

items.title: The ransomware victim in manufacturing is now a $43m company in Europe — the profile moved downmarket and offshore
items.content_text: Black Kite’s 2026 manufacturing and distribution ransomware report counts 1,183 disclosed manufacturing victims in the first seven months of the year — more than the whole of 2023 or 2024, and roughly 40% up on the same period last year. Two shifts matter more than the headline number. European victims grew 85% year on year, from 199 to 369, so this is no longer predominantly a US problem. And the median victim now turns over about $42.9 million, with companies between $10m and $100m making up around 70% of victims whose revenue is known. That is the tier that runs real plant, often single-site, usually with no dedicated OT security staff and frequently sitting inside somebody else’s supply chain — which is how a small supplier’s bad week becomes a large manufacturer’s stoppage.

items.title: The box that decides which VLAN a device lands in can be taken by an unauthenticated request — and it is being taken
items.content_text: Cisco disclosed a maximum-severity authentication bypass in Identity Services Engine and the ISE Passive Identity Connector, tracked as CVE-2026-76460 at CVSS 10.0, caused by insufficient authentication control on an API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the web management interface and gain unauthorised access to the device. Cisco says it was exploited as a zero-day; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 16 September with a federal remediation deadline of 19 September. There is no workaround — upgrading is the only remediation. For industrial sites, ISE is frequently the thing enforcing which devices land on which VLAN, including the segment boundary between enterprise and plant. Whoever holds ISE can rewrite that boundary without touching a switch, a firewall or a controller.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0, Cisco Identity Services Engine; exploited as a zero-day, no workaround

items.title: Three exploited Linux kernel flaws went into KEV with a three-day deadline — and Linux is inside most of your OT edge
items.content_text: CISA added three Linux kernel vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 September, with a federal remediation date of 21 September: CVE-2025-39682 in the kernel TLS receive path (reported as CVSS 9.8), CVE-2026-53266, an out-of-bounds write in the ebtables SNAT target (reported as 8.8), and CVE-2025-39964, a race condition in the AF_ALG crypto socket interface (reported as 7.8). They are local, post-access bugs — the step that turns a foothold into root — rather than remote entry points. No actor, target or sector has been named. The OT angle is where the kernel lives: industrial edge gateways, HMI panel PCs, historians, managed switches and Linux-based security appliances, whose firmware usually lags upstream fixes by months.
tags: KEV — three Linux kernel CVEs added 18 September 2026; three-day federal deadline; local-access flaws

items.title: The block password that protects your control logic can be walked past — and patching the software alone does not fix it
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-260-02 on 17 September covering CVE-2026-15688, an incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm in Mitsubishi Electric GX Works3 and the Motion Control Settings software packaged with it, rated CVSS v4 9.2. All versions are affected. A local attacker who can run the engineering software and modify part of its executable module in memory can authenticate with an invalid block password and then view, tamper with, destroy or delete control programs. This is not a network authentication bypass against a PLC — it is an attack on the protection you rely on to stop a contractor, a temporary engineer or anyone with access to the engineering workstation from reading or altering protected program blocks. The awkward part is the remediation: updating the software is insufficient unless each project is also moved to security version 2.

items.title: One crafted message, no credentials, and an ABB Freelance controller stops
items.content_text: ABB published an advisory on 18 September for CVE-2023-5778 in its Freelance distributed control system: a specially crafted, unauthenticated network message can make AC 700F, AC 800F, AC 900F and Freelance DCP controllers stop. It is scored CVSS 7.5 in ABB’s machine-readable advisory. Affected are Freelance 2013 through 2019 SP1; the fixes are in update rollups that have already shipped, and Freelance 2024 is not affected. ABB reports no exploitation and no prior public disclosure. Freelance is a process DCS found in utilities, water plants and process industry, and many sites run long-lived releases that never took the later rollups. Separately, on 17 September ABB disclosed CVE-2026-18963 (CVSS 9.1) in dynovaPRO, its cloud platform for managing EV chargers, batteries and solar: an unauthenticated forced password reset allowed account takeover. ABB fixed it server-side on 27 August, so customers have nothing to install, but it found 26 suspicious password changes across nine customers and disabled those accounts.

items.title: The authentication on a safety controller can be defeated — and this one runs process shutdown logic in refineries and water plants
items.content_text: Schneider Electric’s September Patch Tuesday set carries a critical authentication flaw in the Modicon M580 and, more pointedly, the M580 Safety range, tracked as CVE-2026-3869 at CVSS v4 9.2. The M580 is not a niche box: it is the ePAC that sits at the centre of a great many continuous-process and utility control systems, and the Safety variant is the controller executing SIL-rated shutdown logic. A weakness in how the controller authenticates a connecting party is the class of defect that lets an attacker on the control network reach the controller as though they were the engineering workstation — which is the step between network access and process consequence. Schneider also fixed high-severity issues in the PowerLogic T300 (the former Easergy T300 RTU) and EcoStruxure IT Data Center Expert, and added Modicon MC80 patch availability to four older advisories.

items.title: An unauthenticated request that carries its own script — a workflow engine is being exploited a month after the proof of concept landed
items.content_text: Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-58138, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Orkes Conductor rated CVSS 9.8. The vulnerability is reached through inline workflow definitions submitted to the workflow API: an attacker embeds malicious JavaScript or Python expressions in a definition, and the engine evaluates them into arbitrary system commands. Versions before 3.30.2 are affected. The timeline is a familiar one — patched in June in version 3.30.2, proof-of-concept code published in early August, first in-the-wild attacks observed by Empirical Security on 21 August, and roughly 1,300 exploitation attempts blocked by one vendor across 8–9 September alone. Conductor is not ICS software, but workflow orchestration engines increasingly sit in industrial data platforms, MES integrations and asset-management pipelines, on the enterprise side of the boundary and with credentials that reach both ways.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-58138, CVSS 9.8, Orkes Conductor workflow orchestration; exploited in the wild since August

items.title: The server that writes the policy for your IT/OT boundary firewalls has an unauthenticated root flaw — not exploited, but the VPN bugs next door already are a warning
items.content_text: Check Point has fixed CVE-2026-91843, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in its Security Management and Log Servers that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code as root. Reporting describes a stack overflow in the login process, triggered by an overly long username in an unauthenticated request. Supported R81.10, R81.20, R82 and R82.10 builds below the listed Jumbo Hotfix takes are affected, as are all R82.20 builds and the end-of-support R81 and R80.x lines; Multi-Domain Server is vulnerable and Smart-1 Cloud is already fixed. The remedy is a LivePatch published under sk1000155. Check Point says there is no indication the flaw has been exploited. It belongs on an OT dashboard because a Check Point management server is often what administers the firewalls between enterprise, DMZ and plant networks — whoever holds it holds the rulebase.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-91843, CVSS 9.8, Check Point Security Management and Log Servers; no exploitation reported

items.title: A control platform for grid compensation equipment, a component shipped since 2020, and confidentiality, integrity and availability all in scope
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-260-03 on 17 September covering vulnerabilities in the Hitachi Energy FACTS Control Platform, the control system for flexible AC transmission systems equipment. The advisory scopes the issue to FACTS control systems that include the GWS component and were deployed from 2020 onwards; deployments without GWS are not affected. Successful exploitation can affect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. The affected product list reads like a transmission substation inventory: SVC Light (STATCOM), fixed series capacitors, thyristor-controlled series capacitors, static VAr compensators, static watt compensators and hybrid synchronous condensers. This is equipment that manages voltage stability and power flow on transmission networks, which puts it in a different consequence category from most advisories on this page. Per reporting on the underlying Hitachi Energy advisory, the flaws are five 2024 CVEs first disclosed for the GWS component, now reaching FACTS through it, with scores up to CVSS 9.9 — including an unauthenticated service exposed on all interfaces.

items.title: Seven advisories in one afternoon: a data-centre edge platform, a UPS shutdown agent, an environment monitor and an electronic logging device
items.content_text: CISA published seven ICS advisories on 17 September, two of which — GX Works3 and Hitachi Energy FACTS — are covered separately on this page. The rest: ICSA-26-260-01 for Bransys ELD, an electronic logging device used in commercial road transport; ICSA-26-260-04 for Schneider Electric Modicon M340 controllers and communication modules, a republication of a 2025 Schneider advisory for an FTP denial-of-service flaw (CVE-2025-6625), fixed in firmware SV3.70; ICSA-26-260-05 for Schneider Electric NetBotz 5 models 750 and 755, the environment monitoring appliances that watch temperature, humidity and door state in control rooms and equipment cabinets; ICSA-26-260-06 for ABB Ability Edgenius, addressing CVE-2026-31431, a Linux kernel flaw where a locally authenticated user or a compromised container workload can escalate to root; and ICSA-26-260-07 for Schneider Electric PowerChute Serial Shutdown, the agent that performs orderly shutdown of servers on UPS battery events. None is exploited. The Edgenius and PowerChute entries are the ones worth a second look, for different reasons.

items.title: Six free federal assessments that small utilities actually used are being withdrawn — and nothing equivalent replaces them
items.content_text: CISA is retiring six no-cost assessments delivered through its regional staff: the Cyber Resilience Review, Cyber Resilience Essentials survey, Ransomware Readiness Assessment, Incident Management Review, External Dependencies Management Assessment and the Cyber Infrastructure Survey. The agency describes the move as removing redundancy in legacy questionnaire-based offerings and points organisations toward the Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals instead. Reporting ties the consolidation to workforce losses of roughly a third of CISA staff since early 2025. The practical loss falls on operators least able to absorb it — small water systems, municipal utilities, rural co-ops and single-site manufacturers that have no security team and used the regional advisor as their only external review. The CPGs are a self-assessment; a visiting advisor was not.
tags: Policy — CISA retires six free critical-infrastructure assessments

items.title: CISA wants critical-infrastructure operators to plant tripwires — and to build them from tools they already own
items.content_text: CISA published guidance on deploying cyber decoys inside critical-infrastructure networks, aimed explicitly at teams that cannot detect an adversary using valid credentials and native administrative tooling. It describes three constructs: honeytokens, which are data elements or logical objects with no legitimate business purpose — fake records, credentials or files — whose use strongly implies unauthorised activity; breadcrumbs, planted references in scripts, documentation, file shares or configuration files that lead an intruder toward a monitored decoy; and honeypots, deliberately vulnerable systems. The instruction that makes this usable is the procurement one: repurpose existing EDR, identity and data-loss-prevention tooling to deploy and monitor decoys rather than buying a deception platform. The stated goal is reduced mean time to detection through high-fidelity alerts.

items.title: The substation risk assessment just got a method, a 36-month clock and a 1,500-foot neighbour test
items.content_text: FERC issued an order on 10 September approving NERC Reliability Standard CIP-014-4, with the Federal Register notice published on 15 September and an effective date of 1 October 2028. The revisions target the part of CIP-014 that NERC concluded lacked rigour and consistency: the R1 risk assessment. Transmission owners must now identify applicable facilities existing or planned to be in service within a 36-month window, aligning the cycle with transmission planning; use a documented risk assessment methodology performing both steady-state and dynamic simulations on at least one system peak load case and one off-peak case; and identify proximate bulk electric system stations and substations within 1,500 feet, fence line to fence line, to evaluate the effect of an attack on adjacent equipment. It is a physical security standard, not a cyber one — but the assessment work, the ownership questions and the budget cycle all land on the same teams.

items.title: Your OT vendor now has 24 hours to tell Brussels a vulnerability in their product is being exploited — and the portal to do it opened the day the clock started
items.content_text: The Cyber Resilience Act’s reporting obligations became applicable on 11 September, and ENISA brought the initial operating capability of its Single Reporting Platform online the same day. Manufacturers placing products with digital elements on the EU market — which covers a great deal of the controller, gateway, HMI, drive and industrial software estate — must now notify actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting product security through one portal, which fans the notification out to the coordinating CSIRT, other affected member states and ENISA. The CRA’s substantive security requirements do not bite until 11 December 2027, and the obligation for open-source stewards starts then too. This is a disclosure-timing change, not a product-security change — but disclosure timing is what determines when you find out.
tags: Regulation — EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations in force since 11 September 2026; ENISA Single Reporting Platform live
